result.title: Dependents, Standard Deduction, and Filing Information
result.text: IRS Publication 501 explains who must file, filing status, dependents, and the standard deduction for individual taxpayers.

nodes.title: Who Must File
nodes.text: Whether you must file a federal income tax return depends on your gross income, filing status, age, and whether you are a dependent.

nodes.title: Filing Status
nodes.text: Your filing status affects your filing requirement, standard deduction, and tax rate. Options include single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household, and qualifying surviving spouse.

nodes.title: Head of Household
nodes.text: You may be able to file as head of household if you are considered unmarried, paid more than half the cost of keeping up a home for the year, and a qualifying person lived with you in the home for more than half the year.

nodes.title: Married Filing Jointly
nodes.text: Married filing jointly combines income and deductions of both spouses on one return.

nodes.title: Married Filing Separately
nodes.text: Married filing separately may limit certain credits and deductions compared to joint filing.

nodes.title: Dependents
nodes.text: Rules for qualifying child and qualifying relative, including relationship, age, residency, support, and joint return tests.

nodes.title: Qualifying Child
nodes.text: A qualifying child must meet relationship, age, residency, support, and joint return tests.

nodes.title: Standard Deduction
nodes.text: Taxpayers who do not itemize deductions may take the standard deduction. Amounts vary by filing status and age or blindness.
